newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nera profits slip but optimistic for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nera profits slip but optimistic for 1997.

text.p: Telecommunications group Nera ASA said on Tuesday higher R&D expenditure and non-recurring costs for restructuring and expansion led to a six percent decline in 1996 operating profits compared with a year ago.
But the company said a healthy order backlog and high production capacity pointed to positive development in 1997.
Nera booked operating profits after research and development (R&D) costs of 171.9 million crowns for last year versus 183 million crowns in 1995.
Pre-tax income was down nearly nine percent at 140.4 million crowns against 153.7 million crowns.

Sales over the 12 months rose 11 percent on 1995 to 2.63 billion crowns and new orders jumped 20 percent to three billion crowns. Nera said new orders and sales in the fourth quarter hit new records at 881 million crowns and 862 million crowns respectively.

New orders for one of the company's core areas, tranmission systems, advanced 68 percent in 1996 to total 1.49 billion crowns. Nera attributed the jump mainly to breakthroughs in the Indian and Latin American markets.
Mobile satellite communications, which include the group's most recent product, the lightweight WorldPhone, attracted new orders of 685 million crowns.

"Recent developments show that the markets for the company's products are still expanding, which was one of the assumptions on which the company's growth strategy was based," Frode Botnevik, Nera's executive chairman, said in a statement.
However, operating expenses rose 11 percent from a year ago including restructuring costs of 60 million crowns and a 28 percent jump in R&D expenditure to 195 million crowns.
Nera said a non-recurring charge of 20 million crowns was booked in the fourth quarter due to extensive reorganisation of the group's radio link plant in Britain.

"The fact that the company has a sound backlog, high production capacity and has launched the world's smallest satellite telephone (WorldPhone) points to a positive development for Nera in 1997," Botnevik said.
"The major part of the restructurings and capacity expansions has now been completed, which will allow us to gradually improve our operating margin."
Nera's share price on the Oslo bourse dropped four crowns in early, light trade to 308 crowns.
